author: priyanka.patel tech editor
title: Total Solar Eclipse 2026: Totality Hits Spain, Iceland and Arctic Regions
text:
A total solar eclipse swept across the globe on August 12, 2026, turning day into night along a narrow path of totality that crossed the extreme arctic of Russia, Greenland, Iceland, the Atlantic Ocean, the northeastern corner of Portugal, northern Spain, and the Balearic Islands. According to nuevarioja.com.ar , the astronomical event marked the second eclipse season and premier celestial phenomenon of 2026. As defined by ninerswire.usatoday.com , a total solar eclipse occurs when the moon passes between the sun and Earth, completely blocking the face of the sun.
Total Solar Eclipse 2026 Plunges Regions Into Darkness The cosmic alignment began at 17 hours and 34 minutes official Spanish time in the Bering Sea and concluded at 21 hours and 58 minutes in the Atlantic Ocean, spanning a total duration of 264 minutes, as reported by telediario.mx . Spanish geographic authorities noted that the maximum point of the eclipse occurred near Iceland, where the peak duration of totality reached two minutes and 18 seconds.
Total Solar Eclipse 2026: Path of Totality to Hit Spain, Iceland and Greenland
Path of Totality Across Spain and Europe Spain served as a primary focal point for viewers, with the path of totality crossing the Iberian Peninsula from west to east. The shadow passed through numerous provincial capitals ranging from A Coruña to Palma, including Oviedo, León, Bilbao, Zaragoza, and Valencia. Local observation schedules in UTC coordinated time included:
León, Spain: Began at 7:32 p.m. and ended at 9:22 p.m. Zaragoza, Spain: Began at 7:34 p.m. and ended at 9:07 p.m. Valencia, Spain: Began at 7:38 p.m. and ended at 9:01 p.m. Reikiavik, Iceland: Began at 4:47 p.m. and ended at 6:47 p.m. Outside the narrow corridor of totality, a partial solar eclipse was visible across large parts of Europe, areas of North America including Alaska, and northwest Africa. Viewers in southern Canada and parts of the United States witnessed a smaller portion of the sun obscured, while regions like Florida did not experience direct visibility of the path but accessed coverage via broadcasts provided by organizations such as univision.com .
2026 Total Solar Eclipse Brings Rare Daytime Darkness to Europe and Spain
An Unprecedented Three-Year Eclipse Sequence in Spain The August 12 event initiated a rare astronomical alignment for Spain, forming the first chapter of a sequential trio of solar eclipses positioning the country as a global astronomical epicentre over a three-year span. Following this event, a second eclipse is scheduled for August 2, 2027, anticipated by the scientific community due to an unusual maximum duration generating over four minutes of total darkness in parts of southern Spain. A third event will follow on January 26, 2028, tracing a ring of fire formation across the Iberian Peninsula from southwest to northeast.
Photo: univision.com Solar Eclipse 2026: Totality in Europe and Partial Views in North America
Safety Guidelines for Solar Observation Space agencies issued strict safety parameters for viewing the progression of the solar event. Observers were advised to utilize specialized solar observation glasses complying with international standard ISO 12312-2 during partial phases. Authorities emphasized that direct viewing without protection is safe exclusively during the brief window of complete totality when the moon completely obscures the bright solar surface. Unfiltered optical devices such as cameras, binoculars, and telescopes were strictly cautioned against unless equipped with dedicated front-mounted solar filters.
